title: Rigveda 5.63: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.63: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.63 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 383r-384r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.63.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 383v
translation.original_text:
1ṛta̍sya gopā̱v adhi̍ tiṣṭhatho̱ ratha̱ṁ satya̍dharmāṇā para̱me vyo̍mani | yam atra̍ mitrāvaru̱ṇāva̍tho yu̱vaṁ tasmai̍ vṛ̱ṣṭir madhu̍mat pinvate di̱vaḥ ||
2sa̱mrājā̍v a̱sya bhuva̍nasya rājatho̱ mitrā̍varuṇā vi̱dathe̍ sva̱rdṛśā̍ | vṛ̱ṣṭiṁ vā̱ṁ rādho̍ amṛta̱tvam ī̍mahe̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī vi ca̍ranti ta̱nyava̍ḥ ||
3sa̱mrājā̍ u̱grā vṛ̍ṣa̱bhā di̱vas patī̍ pṛthi̱vyā mi̱trāvaru̍ṇā̱ vica̍rṣaṇī | ci̱trebhi̍r a̱bhrair upa̍ tiṣṭhatho̱ rava̱ṁ dyāṁ va̍rṣayatho̱ asu̍rasya mā̱yayā̍ ||
translation.text:
1GUARDIANS of Order, ye whose Laws are ever true, in the sublimest heaven your chariot ye ascend. O Mitra-Varuṇa whomsoe'er ye: favour, here, to him the rain with sweetness streameth down from heaven.
2This world's imperial Kings, O Mitra-Varuṇa, ye rule in holy synod, looking on the light. We pray for rain, your boon, and immortality. Through heaven and over earth the thunderers take their way.
3Imperial Kings, strong, Heroes, Lords of earth and heaven, Mitra and Varuṇa, ye ever active Ones, Ye wait on thunder with the many-tinted clouds, and by the Asura's magic power cause Heaven to rain.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 383v (numbered 56v by the scribe) (OPenn image 384, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.63.1 ‹-satya-dharmāṇā parame vi-omani yam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 384r (numbered 57r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.63.4 ‹abhreṇa vṛṣṭyā gūhathaḥ divi›. Verses 5.63.1-3 end on this page; 5.63.1 begins on fol. 383r (numbered 56r by the scribe).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.63.4-7 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 384r
translation.original_text:
4mā̱yā vā̍m mitrāvaruṇā di̱vi śri̱tā sūryo̱ jyoti̍ś carati ci̱tram āyu̍dham | tam a̱bhreṇa̍ vṛ̱ṣṭyā gū̍hatho di̱vi parja̍nya dra̱psā madhu̍manta īrate ||
5ratha̍ṁ yuñjate ma̱ruta̍ḥ śu̱bhe su̱khaṁ śūro̱ na mi̍trāvaruṇā̱ gavi̍ṣṭiṣu | rajā̍ṁsi ci̱trā vi ca̍ranti ta̱nyavo̍ di̱vaḥ sa̍mrājā̱ paya̍sā na ukṣatam ||
6vāca̱ṁ su mi̍trāvaruṇā̱v irā̍vatīm pa̱rjanya̍ś ci̱trāṁ va̍dati̱ tviṣī̍matīm | a̱bhrā va̍sata ma̱ruta̱ḥ su mā̱yayā̱ dyāṁ va̍rṣayatam aru̱ṇām a̍re̱pasa̍m ||
7dharma̍ṇā mitrāvaruṇā vipaścitā vra̱tā ra̍kṣethe̱ asu̍rasya mā̱yayā̍ | ṛ̱tena̱ viśva̱m bhuva̍na̱ṁ vi rā̍jatha̱ḥ sūrya̱m ā dha̍ttho di̱vi citrya̱ṁ ratha̍m ||
translation.text:
4Your magic, Mitra-Varuṇa, resteth in the heaven. The Sun, the wondrous weapon, cometh forth as light. Ye hide him in the sky with cloud and flood of rain, and water-drops, Parjanya! full of sweetness flow.
5The Maruts yoke their easy car for victory, O Mitra-Varuṇa, as a hero in the wars. The thunderers roam through regions varied in their hues. Imperial Kings, bedew us with the milk of heaven.
6Refreshing is your voice, O Mitra-Varuṇa: Parjanya sendeth out a wondrous mighty voice. With magic power the Maruts clothe them with the clouds. Ye Two cause Heaven to rain, the red, the spotless One.
7Wise, with your Law and through the Asura's magic power ye guard the ordinances, Mitra-Varuṇa. Ye by eternal Order govern all the world. Ye set the Sun in heaven as a refulgent car.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 384r (numbered 57r by the scribe) (OPenn image 384, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.63.4 ‹abhreṇa vṛṣṭyā gūhathaḥ divi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 384v (numbered 57v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.64.1 ‹havāmahe pari vrajāiva bāhvoḥ›. Verses 5.63.4-7 end on this page; 5.63.4 begins on fol. 383v (numbered 56v by the scribe).
